scene: At a muddy Viking Age trading place on a grey shore, Colm, huge and expressive in the foreground (young adult man, short dark hair, no beard, cream round face, rough undyed grey-brown wool tunic with a rope belt, worn brown shoes, black mitten hands), stares in stunned disbelief at a big wooden-beamed merchant's balance scale beside him: on one pan a small heap of jagged hacksilver, the other pan empty and waiting. Behind the scale Hallvard (big man, black beard, dark blue cloak with a brown fur collar, round silver brooch) counts the silver with a satisfied look, while a dealer with a pile of furs and salt sacks shrugs. Longships and plank stalls behind, no ropes or chains on any person. Visible hardship: a man's whole life reduced to a few pieces of silver.

At a wooden farm gate in a snowy western Norwegian valley, Colm, huge and expressive in the foreground (short dark hair, no beard, rough undyed grey-brown tunic, black mitten hands), holds a scruffy escaped sheep on a rope and looks with a hurt, frozen stare at Eirik behind the fence (red-brown hair and beard, teal tunic, brown cloak, a long pale scar on his forearm), who takes the sheep with a polite, blank smile and no recognition at all; Aslaug (pale flax headcloth, mauve dress) watches from the turf-roofed longhouse door. Visible hardship: the captive faces the oarsman of the raid, who has already forgotten him.
